ESSENCE STATEMENT FOR HISTORY AND CITIZENSHIP
The History and Citizenship curriculum in Senior School is designed to help learners understand the world by building on four
broad thematic strands. It emphasizes social justice, governance, civic responsibility, and the evolution of societal norms. Through
studying historical events, learners learn to analyse human behaviour and understand the impact of past decisions. This approach
sharpens their critical thinking and prepares them to interpret the present with depth and empathy.

Citizenship education complements history by encouraging learners to become active, informed members of society. It teaches
them about their rights and responsibilities, instilling a strong sense of civic duty. Through skills like dialogue, collaboration, and
ethical decision-making, learners are equipped for participation in democratic life. This empowers them to not only understand
society but also contribute meaningfully to it.

By exploring past struggles for justice and equality, learners find role models and lessons that encourage civic advocacy. Historical
examples such as the abolition of slavery and the civil rights movement show how individuals can drive social change. These
narratives inspire learners to stand against modern injustices and champion fairness. History thus becomes a tool for empowerment
and ethical action.

The integration of History and Citizenship helps learners see the relevance of the past in shaping the future. This interdisciplinary
approach fosters empathy, resilience, and responsible citizenship. Assessments further support this learning by focusing on both
academic growth and social-emotional development. Ultimately, learners are prepared to face contemporary challenges with
knowledge, purpose, and a strong sense of societal responsibility.

x

GENERAL LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR HISTORY AND CITIZENSHIP
By the end of Senior Secondary School, the learner should be able to:
1. Demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of key themes in Kenyan history and citizenship.
2. Explore Kenya's position in regional and global contexts, recognizing its contributions to peace-building, governance, and
international cooperation.
3. Demonstrate a deep understanding of the diverse African Civilisations, their cultural contributions, and the historical processes
of colonization, independence, and post-colonial transformation.
4. Critically analyse the social, political, and economic changes in African societies, recognizing the lasting impact of colonialism
and the ongoing efforts towards African unity, development, and self-determination.
5. Examine the role of African citizens in promoting good governance, peace-building, and sustainable development, both at
national and regional levels.
6. Analyse significant global events, such as revolutions, wars, and the rise of empires, and assess their impact on shaping modern
societies, international relations, and world systems.
7. Examine key global movements and institutions that promote equality, democracy, and peace, and understand the roles of
individuals and nations in addressing contemporary global challenges such as poverty, climate change, and conflict resolution.
8. Conduct research and analyse the major political, social, and technological transformations of the contemporary world.
9. Explore the impact of globalization, the rise of digital technologies, and the evolution of global economies, while understanding
the role of contemporary social movements in advocating for human rights, equality, and environmental sustainability.
10. Exhibit an understanding of the responsibilities of citizenship in the modern world.
11. Recognise the role of individuals in democratic processes, social justice advocacy, and global governance, and actively engage
in discussions on how to promote civic participation, social equity, and peace in their communities and the wider world.

FOREWORD
The Government of Kenya (GoK) is committed to ensuring that policy objectives for Education, Training and Research meet the aspirations
of the Kenya Constitution 2010, the Kenya Vision 2030, National Curriculum Policy 2019, the United Nations Sustainable Development
Goals (SDGs) and the Regional and Global conventions to which Kenya is a signatory.

Towards achieving the mission of Basic Education, the Ministry of Education (MoE) embarked on a reform process that culminated in the
adoption of a Competency Based Education (CBE) system in 2017. This came after extensive research, stakeholder engagement international
benchmarking and consideration of the 21st Century socio-economic realities. CBE in Kenya adopted a 2-6-3-3 structure where the numbers
indicate the years learners take at various levels in Basic Education (Pre-Primary, Primary, Junior School and Senior School; respectively).
CBE has for critical elements: The Competency Based Curriculum (CBC), Pedagogy (teaching and learning), Resources and the Competency
Based Assessment. The MoE oversees the provision of resources while the other components (Curriculum, Pedagogy and Assessment are
handled by the Kenya Institute of Curriculum Development, (KICD), Teachers Service Commission, (TSC) and the Kenya National
Examinations Council (KNEC); respectively.

KICD has successfully developed curriculum designs that have been used in the implementation of the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC)
for the Pre-Primary, Primary and Juniors School levels. The first cohort of learners pursuing the CBC will transit to Senior School (Grades
10-12) in 2026. The curriculum designs at this level are expected to facilitate learners to acquire relevant knowledge, skills, values and attitudes
(competencies) in preparation for tertiary education and the world of work. I urge all agencies of the GoK and other stakeholders in Education
to use the designs to plan for effective and efficient implementation of Competency Based Education.

MR. JULIUS MIGOS OGAMBA
CABINET SECRETARY,
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION

PREFACE
The Ministry of Education (MoE) through the State Department for Basic Education, has been implementing the Competency Based Education
(CBE) since the adoption of the Basic Education Curriculum Framework (KICD, 2017) during the national convention in January 2017. The Kenya
Institute of Curriculum Development (KICD) developed Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) designs that were used for pilot studies in 2017 and
2018 before the roll-out at Pre-Primary and Primary Early Year (Grades 1 to 3 in 2019. The curriculum was then introduced in the subsequent grades
through a phase in –phase out strategy, to ensure a smooth transition. Currently, the first cohort of CBC learners are at Grade 9 – the last grade at
Junior School. The implementation of CBE has since benefited immensely from the recommendations of the Presidential Working Party on
Education Reforms (PWPER) that were released in August, 2023 and fully implemented, in terms of curriculum designs.

Grade 10 is the entry class of the Senior School (SS) in Basic Education, a very critical level where learners shall have the opportunity to focus on
pathways, tracks and subjects of their choices guided by the potentials demonstrated at earlier levels. The Senior School shall; therefore, form a
foundation for further education and training and/or initial competencies for the Industry. This is an important step in the realisation of the Vision
and Mission of the curriculum reforms as enshrined in the Sessional Paper No. I of 2019 whose title is: Towards Realizing Quality, Relevant and
Inclusive Education and Training for Sustainable Development in Kenya.

The Grade 10 curriculum designs, like the designs for earlier levels, are anchored on the Kenyan National Goals of Education. They also present
essence statements, general and specific expected learning outcomes as well as strands and sub strands for the learning areas. The designs also outline
suggested learning experiences, key inquiry questions, core competencies, Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCIs), values and suggested
assessment.

The Ministry of Education, through the State Department for Basic Education commits to provide resources and relevant guidelines for a smooth
implementation of the CBC. It is expected that the designs will guide teachers to effectively facilitate learners to attain the expected learning outcomes
for Grade 10 specifically and Senior School in general.

NATIONAL GOALS OF EDUCATION
Education in Kenya should:
1. Foster nationalism and patriotism and promote national unity
The people of Kenya belong to different communities, races and religions, but these differences need not divide them. They must
be able to live and interact as Kenyans. It is a paramount duty of education to help young people acquire this sense of nationhood
by resolving conflicts and promoting positive attitudes of mutual respect, to live together in harmony and foster patriotism, and
make a positive contribution to the life of the nation.

2. Promote the social, economic, technological, and industrial needs for national development
Education should prepare the youth of the country to play an effective and productive role in the life of the nation.
a) Social Needs
Education in Kenya must prepare children for changes in attitudes and relationships necessary for the smooth progress of a
rapidly developing modern economy. Rapid modernisation is bound to lead to a silent social revolution, and education should
assist our youth in adapting to this change.
b) Economic Needs
Education in Kenya should produce citizens with the skills, knowledge, expertise, and personal qualities required to support a
growing economy. Kenya is building a modern and independent economy that needs an adequate and relevant domestic
workforce.
c) Technological and Industrial Needs
Education in Kenya should provide learners with the necessary skills and attitudes for industrial development. Kenya recognises
the rapid industrial and technological changes taking place, especially in the developed world. We can only contribute to this
development if our education system is deliberately focused on the knowledge, skills, and attitudes that will prepare our young
people for these changing global trends.

3. Promote individual development and self-fulfilment
Education should provide opportunities for the fullest development of individual talents and personality. It should help children to
develop their potential interests and abilities. A vital aspect of individual development is the building of character.

v

4. Promote sound moral and religious values.
Education should provide for the development of knowledge, skills and attitudes that will enhance the acquisition of sound moral
values and help children to grow up into self-disciplined, self-reliant, and integrated citizens.

5. Promote social equality and responsibility.
Education should promote social equality and foster a sense of social responsibility within an education system that provides equal
educational opportunities for all. It should give all children varied and challenging opportunities for collective activities and
corporate social service irrespective of gender, ability, or geographical environment.

6. Promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures.
Education should instil in the youth of Kenya an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in contemporary
society. Children should be able to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must follow rapid
development to build a stable and modern society.

7. Promote international consciousness and foster positive attitudes towards other nations.
Kenya is part of the international community. It is part of the complicated and interdependent network of peoples and nations.
Education should therefore lead the youth of the country to accept membership of this international community with all the
obligations and responsibilities, rights, and benefits that this membership entails.

8. Promote positive attitudes towards good health and environmental protection.
Education should inculcate in young people the value of good health for them to avoid indulging in activities that will lead to
physical or mental ill health. It should foster positive attitudes towards environmental development and conservation. It should
lead the youth of Kenya to appreciate the need for a healthy environment.

vi

THE SENIOR SCHOOL IN THE COMPETENCY BASED CURRICULUM
Senior School is the fourth level of Basic Education in the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) that learners shall proceed to after the Pre-
Primary School, Primary School and Junior School levels. The essence of Senior School is to offer learners a pre-tertiary/university/pre-career
experience in which the learners have an opportunity to choose pathways, tracks and subjects where they shall have demonstrated interest
and/or potential at the earlier levels. Senior School comprises three years of education for learners generally in the 16-18 years age bracket
and lays the foundation for further education and training at the tertiary level and the world of work. In the CBC vision, learners exiting this
level are expected to be engaged, empowered and ethical citizens ready to participate in the socio-economic development of the nation.

At this level, learners shall take seven (7) learning areas as recommended by the Presidential Working Party on Educational Reforms (PWPER,
2023). These shall comprise four compulsory learning areas namely: English, Kiswahili, Essential Mathematics/Core Mathematics and
Community Service Learning (CSL). Learners will choose between Core Mathematics (for learners pursuing the Science Technology
Engineering and Mathematics Pathway) and Essential Mathematics (for learners pursuing the non-STEM pathways). The learner will select
three learning areas depending on their career choice, aptitude, interest and personality with guidance by the career teacher at Senior School.

LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR SENIOR SCHOOL
By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:
1. Communicate effectively and utilise information and communication technology across varied contexts.
2. Apply mathematical, logical and critical thinking skills for problem solving.
3. Apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve problems.
4. Exploit individual talents for leisure, self-fulfilment, career growth, further education and training.
5. Uphold national, moral and religious values and apply them in day-to-day life.
6. Apply and promote health care strategies in day-to-day life.
7. Protect, preserve and improve the environment for sustainability.
8. Demonstrate active local and global citizenship for harmonious co-existence.
9. Demonstrate appreciation of diversity in people and cultures.
10. Manage pertinent and contemporary issues responsibly.

ESSENCE STATEMENT
The Senior School English curriculum is designed to build upon the foundational linguistic and communicative competencies
developed at the Junior School level. These early skills in listening, speaking, reading, and writing provide a solid base for learners
to engage with English as a tool for communication, a medium of instruction, and a subject of academic study.
At the Senior School level, the English language educators are expected to use transformative pedagogical approaches grounded
in contemporary linguistic and language learning theories. Teachers could employ methodologies such as Experiential Learning,
Problem-Based Learning (PBL), Project-Based Learning, Collaborative Learning, Reflective Learning, and Communicative
Language Teaching coupled with the innovative use of ICTs to pique the learner’s interest and enhance proficiency. Classroom
strategies may include journaling, peer and self-assessment, lesson recordings for reflection, case studies, storytelling, simulations,
role play, hot seating, reader’s theatre and structured debates. These approaches are intended to create dynamic, learner-centred
environments that promote both linguistic competency and metacognitive awareness. Beyond the classroom, educators are
encouraged to facilitate learners’ participation in non-formal and informal language-rich activities such as drama and music
festivals, public speaking events, debates, and involvement in clubs and societies. These experiences provide authentic contexts
for language use and help learners connect English to real-world applications.
Given the status of English as the global lingua franca in domains such as diplomacy, commerce, technology, and international
relations, proficiency in the language opens diverse academic and career pathways, by the end of Senior School. These advanced
English language skills are necessary for further education and professional pursuits in fields such as law, journalism, marketing,
advertising, public relations, editing, research, linguistics, teaching, lexicography, translation, and the performing arts.

x

GENERAL SUBJECT LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR ENGLISH
By the end of the course, the learner should be able to:
1. use verbal and nonverbal cues appropriately for speaking fluency,
2. listen to varied oral texts for comprehension,
3. speak on a wide range of subjects fluently and confidently,
4. apply knowledge of grammar in oral and written texts,
5. develop a wide range of vocabulary for use in formal and informal discourse,
6. read a range of texts for information and pleasure including texts from contrasting times and cultures,
7. write creative, functional, and argumentative texts for varied purposes and audiences,
8. utilize ICTs innovatively to convey oral and written information.

ulipitisha muundo wa 2-6-3-3, ambapo tarakimu hizo zinaonyesha idadi ya miaka ambayo wanafunzi hutumia katika viwango
mbalimbali vya Elimu ya Msingi (Chekechea, Shule ya Msingi, Shule ya Junia na Daraja ya Juu ya Shule za Upili mtawalia). CBE
ina vipengele vinne muhimu: Mtaala wa Kiumilisi (CBC), Mbinu za Ufudishaji (ufundishaji na ujifunzaji), Rasilimali, na Tathmini
ya Kiumilisi. Wizara ya Elimu husimamia utoaji wa rasilimali huku vipengele vingine (Mtaala, Mbinu za Ufudishaji na Tathmini)
vikisimamiwa na Taasisi ya Ukuzaji Mitaala Kenya (KICD), Tume ya Tume ya Kuwaajiri Walimu (TSC), na Baraza la Kitaifa la
Mitihani nchini Kenya (KNEC); mtawalia.

KICD imefanikiwa kuandaa mitaala ambayo imetumika katika utekelezaji wa Mtaala wa Kiumilisi (CBC) katika kiwango cha
Chekechea, Shule ya Msingi, Shule ya Junia na Daraja ya Juu ya Shule za Upili. Kundi la kwanza la wanafunzi wanaofanya mfumo
wa CBC litajiunga na Daraja ya Juu ya Shule za Upili (Gredi ya 10 -12) mwaka 2026. Mitaala katika kiwango hiki inatarajiwa
kuwezesha wanafunzi kupata maarifa, ujuzi, maadili na mitazamo inayofaa (umilisi) ili kuwaandaa kwa ajili ya elimu ya juu na
ulimwengu wa kazi.Ninatoa wito kwa mashirika yote ya serikali ya Kenya na wadau wengine wa elimu kutumia mitaala hii kuandaa
utekelezaji fanifu na wenye tija wa Eimu wa Kiumilisi.

DIBAJI YA KATIBU MKUU
Wizara ya Elimu (MoE), kupitia Idara ya Serikali ya Elimu ya Msingi, imekuwa ikitekeleza Mtaala wa Kiumilisi (CBC) tangu kupitishwa kwa
Mfumo wa Mtaala wa Elimu ya Msingi (KICD, 2017) wakati wa mkutano wa kitaifa mnamo Januari 2017. Taasisi ya Ukuzaji Mitaala Kenya (KICD)
imeandaa mitaala ambayo ilitumika katika majaribio ya awali mwaka wa 2017 na 2018 kabla kuanzishwa rasmi katika kiwango cha Shule ya
Chekechea, Shule ya Msingi (Gredi 1 hadi 3) mwaka wa 2019. Mtaala huo kisha ulianzishwa katika gredi zinazofuata kwa kutumia mikakati ya
awamu kwa awamu ili kuhakikisha mpito mzuri. Kwa sasa, kundi la kwanza la wanafunzi wa Mtaala wa Kiumilisi wako katika Gredi ya 9 – gredi
ya mwisho katika Shule ya Junia.Utekelezaji wa Elimu ya Kiumilisi pia umenufaika pakubwa kutokana na mapendekezo ya Jopo Kazi la Rais kuhusu
Mabadiliko ya Elimu (PWPER), ambayo yalitolewa mnamo Agosti 2023 na kutekelezwa kikamilifu, hasa katika kuandaa mitaala.

Gredi ya 10 ni darasa la kwanza katika Daraja ya Juu ya Shule za Upili katika Elimu ya Msingi, kiwango muhimu sana ambapo wanafunzi watapata
fursa ya kuangazia njia na mwelekeo wa masomo kulingana na vipaji na uchaguzi wao, kama ulivyoonyeshwa katika viwango vya awali. Kwa hivyo,
Daraja ya Juu ya Shule za Upili itaunda msingi wa elimu ya juu zaidi na/au ukuzaji wa umilisi wa awali kwa sekta ya viwanda. Hii ni hatua muhimu
katika kufanikisha ruwaza ya mageuzi ya mtaala, ambayo inalenga kuandaa raia waliohusishwa, wenye uwezo, na waadilifu. Ruwaza na mwito wa
Mtaala wa Kiumilisi zimebainishwa katika Sheria Nambari 1 ya mwaka 2019, yenye kichwa: Kuelekea Utekelezaji wa Elimu na Mafunzo Bora,
Yanayohusiana na Mahitaji na Yaliyojumuishi kwa Maendeleo Endelevu nchini Kenya.

Mitaala ya Gredi ya 10, kama mitaala ya viwango vya awali, imejiegemeza kwenye Malengo ya Kitaifa ya Elimu Nchini Kenya. Pia huwasilisha
kauli kiini, matokeo ya jumla na maalum pamoja na mada na mada ndogo za masomo mbalimbali. Mitaala pia inaeleza shughuli za ujifunzaji,maswali
dadisi,umilisi wa kimsingi, masuala mtambuko, maadili na mapendekezo ya tathmini.

Wizara ya Elimu, kupitia Idara ya Serikali ya Elimu ya Msingi, imejitolea kutoa rasilimali na miongozo inayofaa ili kuhakikisha utekelezaji mzuri
wa Mtaala wa Kiumilisi. Inatarajiwa kwamba mitaala hii itaongoza walimu kuhakikisha ubora wa utekelezaji wa mtaala ili kuwawezesha wanafunzi
kufanikisha matokeo maalum yanayotarajiwa katika Gredi ya 10 mahsusi na Daraja ya Juu ya Shule za Upili kwa ujumla.

SHUKRANI
Sheria Nambari 4 ya 2013 ya Taasisi ya Ukuzaji Mitaala Kenya inaipa mamlaka Taasisi kukuza mitaala, program na nyenzo za utekelezaji
mtaala kwa elimu ya msingi na taasisi za elimu na mafunzo. Mchakato wa ukuzaji mtaala wa kiwango chochote cha elimu huhusisha utafiti
wa kina, ulinganishi wa kimataifa na uhusishaji mkubwa wa wadau. Kupitia kwa mchakato uliopangwa kikamilifu na wa mashauriano, KICD
ilibuni Mtaala wa Kiumilisi (CBC) kama ilivyoelezwa katika Utaratibu wa Mtaala wa Elimu ya Msingi (KICD, 2017), ambayo inakidhi
mahitaji ya Karne ya 21, Malengo ya Maendeleo Endelevu ya Umoja wa Mataifa (SDGs), Ajenda ya Afrika 2063, Itifaki ya Jumuiya ya Afrika
Mashariki (EAC) na malengo yaliyo katika Katiba ya Kenya ya 2010 na Ruwaza ya Kenya 2030.
KICD hupata ufadhili kutoka kwa Serikali ya Kenya ili kuwezesha ufikiaji kikamilifu wa majukumu na utekelezaji wa mipango ya Serikali
na Sekta za Wizara ya Elimu. Taasisi pia inapata msaada kutoka kwa washirika wa maendeleo unaolenga miradi mahususi. Mitaala ya Gredi
ya 10 imeandaliwa kwa ufadhili wa Benki ya Dunia na Serikali ya Kenya kupitia mpango wa Kenya Primary Education Equity in Learning
Programme (KPEEL); ulio chini ya uelekezi wa Wizara ya Elimu. Kwa hivyo, Taasisi inatoa shukrani za dhati kwa msaada kutoka kwa
Serikali ya Kenya kupitia Wizara ya Elimu na washirika wengine (hasa Benki la Dunia) wa maendeleo kwa sera, raslimali na mikakati. Taasisi

Pia tunatambua wakuza mitaala wa KICD na wafanyakazi wengine, walimu wote, wakufunzi walioshiriki kama wanajopo, taasisi
zilizoshiriki na wawakilishi wa wadau mbalimbali kwa mchango wao katika uandaaji wa mitaala ya Gredi ya 10. Kuhusiana na hili,
tunashukuru msaada wa Wakuu Watendaji wa Tume ya Kuwaajiri Walimu (TSC), Baraza la Mitihani la Kitaifa la Kenya (KNEC), na

iii

MALENGO YA KITAIFA YA ELIMU NCHINI KENYA
Elimu nchini Kenya inatakiwa:
1. Kukuza na kustawisha utaifa, uzalendo na kuendeleza umoja wa kitaifa
Nchini Kenya kuna jamii zenye mila, dini na tamaduni mbalimbali lakini tofauti hizi hazifai kuzitenganisha. Lazima waweze kuishi
na kutangamana kama Wakenya. Elimu ina jukumu kuu la kuwezesha vijana kujenga hisia za uzalendo na utaifa kwa kutatua
mivutano na kukuza mielekeo chanya ya kuheshimiana. Mielekeo hii itawawezesha wanajamii kuishi pamoja kwa utangamano na
kujenga uzalendo ili kuchangia ukuaji wa taifa.
2. Kukidhi mahitaji ya kijamii, kiuchumi, kiteknolojia na viwanda yanayochangia maendeleo ya kitaifa
Elimu inafaa kuwaandaa vijana wa taifa la Kenya kutekeleza wajibu wenye umuhimu katika maisha nchini.
a) Mahitaji ya kijamii
Elimu nchini Kenya lazima iwatayarishe vijana kwa mabadiliko ya mielekeo na mahusiano ambayo yanahitajika kwa maendeleo
ya haraka ya uchumi wa kisasa. Kuna uwezekano wa kuwa na mageuzi taratibu ya kijamii kutokana na maendeleo ya haraka ya
usasa. Elimu inapaswa kuwasaidia vijana kujirekekebisha kutokana na mabadiliko haya.
b) Mahitaji ya kiuchumi
Elimu nchini Kenya inafaa kukuza raia walio na stadi, maarifa, ujuzi na sifa za kibinafsi zinazohitajika kuhimili maendeleo ya
kiuchumi. Kenya inajenga uchumi huru na wa kisasa ambao unahitaji wafanyakazi wa kutosha, walio na maarifa yanayohitajika
humu nchini.
c) Mahitaji ya kiteknolojia na ya kiviwanda
Elimu nchini Kenya inafaa kuwapa vijana stadi na mielekeo inayohitajika kwa maendeleo ya kiviwanda.Kenya inatambua
mabadiliko ya haraka ya kiviwanda na kiteknolojia yanayofanyika, hasa katika ulimwengu ulioendelea. Tunaweza kuwa
sehemu ya maendeleo haya ikiwa mfumo wetu wa elimu utalenga kimakusudi maarifa, stadi na mielekeo itakayotayarisha vijana
kwa mabadiliko yanayoendelea ulimwenguni.

3. Kutoa nafasi ya kujiendeleza na kujitosheleza
Elimu inapaswa kuwezesha kutambua, kukuza na kuimarisha vipawa vya kila mmoja ili kuweza kujiendeleza na kujitosheleza.
Inafaa kuwawezesha watoto kukuza uwezo wao. Kipengele muhimu cha maendeleo ya kibinafsi ni ujenzi wa tabia ifaayo.

v

4. Kuwawezesha wananchi kuimarisha maadili na amali za kijamii na kidini
Elimu inakusudiwa kukuza maarifa, stadi na mielekeo itakayoimarisha upataji wa maadili na kuwasaidia watoto kukua wakiwa
wenye nidhamu, wanaojitegemea na raia wakamilifu.
5. Kuimarisha usawa wa kijamii na uwajibikaji
Usawa wa kijamii kwa mfano, usawa wa kijinsia huimarika watu wa jamii na jinsia zote wanapopata elimu sawa.
Elimu inafaa ikuze usawa wa kijamii na uwajibikaji wa kijamii kutokana na mfumo wa elimu unaowezesha fursa sawa ya elimu
kwa wote. Inafaa kuwapa watoto wote fursa mbalimbali na zenye changamoto zitakazowawezesha kutoa huduma jumuishi za
kijamii bila kujali jinsia, uwezo au mazingira ya kijiografia.

6. Kukuza uthamini wa tamaduni mbalimbali nchini Kenya
Elimu inafaa kuwapa vijana uelewa wa tamaduni za kale na za sasa na nafasi yazo katika jamii ya kisasa. Vijana wanafaa
kuambatanisha maadili ya tamaduni bora na mahitaji yanayobadilika kulingana na maendeleo yanayotokea ili kujenga jamii thabiti
ya kisasa.
7. Kuimarisha utambuzi wa uhusiano wa kimataifa na kukuza mwelekeo chanya kwa mataifa mengine
Kenya kama nchi mojawapo ya jamii ya kimataifa inakusudia elimu iwaelekeze Wakenya kutambua na kuthamini mahusiano ya
kimataifa kwa kuzingatia mikataba, uwajibikaji, haki na manufaa yanayoambatana na ushirika huo.
8. Kustawisha mwelekeo chanya kuhusu afya bora na uhifadhi wa mazingira
Elimu inakusudiwa kujenga mielekeo ifaayo miongoni mwa vijana kuhusu udumishaji wa afya bora na mazingira kwa kujiepusha
na mienendo inayoweza kudhuru afya ya mwili na akili. Aidha, inafaa kuimarisha mielekeo chanya kuhusu ukuzaji na uhifadhi wa
mazingira na kuwaelekeza vijana kuthamini usafi wa mazingira.

vi

DARAJA YA JUU SHULE ZA UPILI KATIKA MTAALA WA KIUMILISI
Daraja ya Juu ya Shule za Upili, ni kiwango cha nne cha Elimu ya Msingi katika Mtaala wa Kiumilisi (CBC) ambayo wanafunzi
watajiunga nayo baada ya kumaliza Chekechea, Shule ya Msingi, na Shule ya Junia. Lengo kuu la Daraja ya Shule za Upili ni kuwapa
wanafunzi uzoefu wa awali wa chuo kikuu au taaluma, ambapo wanafunzi wanapata fursa ya kuchagua mielekeo na nyanja
wanazovutiwa nazo na walizoonyesha uwezo katika viwango vya awali. Daraja ya Juu ya Shule za Upili inajumuisha miaka mitatu ya
masomo kwa wanafunzi walio kati ya umri wa miaka 16-18 na huweka msingi wa elimu ya juu zaidi, mafunzo ya kitaaluma, na
ulimwengu wa kazi. Katika ruwaza ya Mtaala wa Kiumilisi, wanafunzi watakaohitimu katika kiwango hiki wanatarajiwa kuwa raia
waliohusishwa, waliowezeshwa, na waadilifu walio tayari kushiriki katika maendeleo ya kijamii na kiuchumi ya taifa.

Katika kiwango hiki, wanafunzi watajifunza masomo saba (7) kama yalivyopendekezwa na Kamati ya Rais ya Mageuzi ya Elimu
(PWPER, 2023). Masomo haya yanajumuisha masomo manne ya lazima ambayo ni: English, Kiswahili, Essential Mathematics/Core
Mathematics na Community Service Learning – CSL. Wanafunzi watachagua kati ya Core Mathematics (kwa wanafunzi wanaofuatilia
mkondo wa STEM) na Essential Mathematics (kwa wanafunzi wanaofuatilia mikondo isiyo ya STEM). Wanafunzi watachagua masomo
mengine matatu kulingana na chaguo la taaluma, vipaji, mapendeleo yao kwa somo fulani, na haiba zao, wakisaidiwa na mwalimu wao
wa Daraja ya juu shule za upili.

MATOKEO YA DARAJA YA JUU SHULE ZA UPILI
Kufikia mwisho wa Daraja ya Juu ya Shule za Upili, mwanafunzi aweze:
1. Kuwasiliana ipasavyo na kutumia teknolojia ya habari na mawasiliano katika miktadha mbalimbali.
2. Kutumia maarifa ya kihisabati, kimantiki na uwazaji kina katika utatuzi wa matatizo.
3. Kutumia maarifa ya kimsingi ya utafiti na sayansi kudhibiti mazingira yake na kutatua matatizo.
4. Kutumia vizuri vipaji mbalimbali kwa ajili ya burudani, kujiendeleza kitaaluma, kielimu pamoja na kimafunzo.
5. Kudumisha tunu za kitaifa, kimaadili na kidini katika maisha ya kila siku.
6. Kutumia na kuendeleza mikakati ya matunzo ya kiafya katika maisha ya kila siku.
7. Kulinda, kuhifadhi na kuboresha mazingira kwa ajili ya uendelevu.
8. Kudhihirisha uraia wa kitaifa na wa kimataifa kwa ajili ya utangamano wa kindugu.
9. Kuonyesha uthamini wa tofauti za watu na tamaduni.
10. Kuonyesha uwajibikaji katika kushughulikia masuala mtambuko.

KAULI KIINI
Somo la Fasihi ya Kiswahili katika Daraja ya Juu ya Shule za Upili linaendeleza maarifa na ujuzi ambao mwanafunzi amepata
katika Shule ya Junia. Lengo kuu ni kumwezesha mwanafunzi kupanua uelewa wake kuhusu fasihi, si tu kama sanaa ya lugha bali
pia kama chombo cha kuelewa na kushirikiana na tamaduni mbalimbali. Mabadiliko haya kutoka Shule ya Junia hadi daraja ya
juu huambatana na upanuzi wa dhana, stadi, na mwelekeo wa kifasihi. Wanafunzi hujifunza kwa kina kuhusu tanzu mbalimbali
za fasihi kama vile ushairi, riwaya, tamthilia, hadithi fupi, kazi za kihalisia na fasihi simulizi. Somo hili hulenga kukuza uwezo
wa mwanafunzi wa kusoma kwa kina, kutathmini na kuhakiki kazi za fasihi kwa kuzingatia muktadha wa kijamii, kiutamaduni na
kihistoria. Aidha, somo hili huwasaidia wanafunzi kutambua nafasi ya fasihi kama sanaa ya lugha na kama chombo cha
kuwasilisha, kuhifadhi, na kuendeleza maadili na tamaduni za jamii mbalimbali.

Mbinu za ujifunzaji katika somo hili zinalenga kumwandaa mwanafunzi kwa hatua inayofuata ya kielimu na kimaisha. Ufundishaji
huhusisha ushirikishwaji wa wanafunzi kupitia mijadala ya kina, uchambuzi wa matini, uandishi wa kazi za kiubunifu na
utekelezaji wa miradi ya kifasihi. Vilevile, wanafunzi watashiriki matukio ya kifasihi kama vile maonyesho ya kazi za kibunilizi,
mashindano ya ushairi na makongamano ya kielimu ili kukuza stadi za uwasilishaji na kuwapa wanafunzi uwezo wa kufikiri kwa
kina, kuwasiliana kwa ufasaha, na kushirikiana na wengine katika mazingira tofauti ya kijamii na kitaaluma. Hali hii huwajengea
misingi imara ya kujiamini na kuwa raia wenye mchango chanya katika jamii yao na ulimwenguni kwa jumla.

Kufikia mwisho wa kozi, mwanafunzi anatarajiwa kuwa amefikia kiwango cha juu cha umahiri katika Fasihi ya Kiswahili. Hali
hii itamfungulia fursa za ajira katika taaluma kama vile uandishi wa habari,tafsiri, uchapishaji, utafiti wa kifasihi, ufundishaji,
sanaa za maonyesho, burudani na utangazaji.

FOREWORD
The Government of Kenya (GoK) is committed to ensuring that policy objectives for Education, Training and Research meet the aspirations
of the Kenya Constitution 2010, the Kenya Vision 2030, National Curriculum Policy 2019, the United Nations Sustainable Development
Goals (SDGs) and the Regional and Global conventions to which Kenya is a signatory.

Towards achieving the mission of Basic Education, the Ministry of Education (MoE) embarked on a reform process that culminated in the
adoption of a Competency Based Education (CBE) system in 2017. This came after extensive research, stakeholder engagement international
benchmarking and consideration of the 21st Century socio-economic realities. CBE in Kenya adopted a 2-6-3-3 structure where the numbers
indicate the years learners take at various levels in Basic Education (Pre-Primary, Primary, Junior School and Senior School; respectively).
CBE has for critical elements: The Competency Based Curriculum (CBC), Pedagogy (teaching and learning), Resources and the Competency
Based Assessment. The MoE oversees the provision of resources while the other components (Curriculum, Pedagogy and Assessment are
handled by the Kenya Institute of Curriculum Development, (KICD), Teachers Service Commission, (TSC) and the Kenya National
Examinations Council (KNEC); respectively.

KICD has successfully developed curriculum designs that have been used in the implementation of the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC)
for the Pre-Primary, Primary and Juniors School levels. The first cohort of learners pursuing the CBC will transit to Senior School (Grades
10-12) in 2026. The curriculum designs at this level are expected to facilitate learners to acquire relevant knowledge, skills, values and attitudes
(competencies) in preparation for tertiary education and the world of work. I urge all agencies of the GoK and other stakeholders in Education
to use the designs to plan for effective and efficient implementation of Competency Based Education.

PREFACE
The Ministry of Education (MoE) through the State Department for Basic Education, has been implementing the Competency Based Education
(CBE) since the adoption of the Basic Education Curriculum Framework (KICD, 2017) during the national convention in January 2017. The Kenya
Institute of Curriculum Development (KICD) developed Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) designs that were used for pilot studies in 2017 and
2018 before the roll-out at Pre-Primary and Primary Early Year (Grades 1 to 3 in 2019. The curriculum was then introduced in the subsequent grades
through a phase in –phase out strategy, to ensure a smooth transition. Currently, the first cohort of CBC learners are at Grade 9 – the last grade at
Junior School. The implementation of CBE has since benefited immensely from the recommendations of the Presidential Working Party on
Education Reforms (PWPER) that were released in August, 2023 and fully implemented, in terms of curriculum designs.

Grade 10 is the entry class of the Senior School (SS) in Basic Education, a very critical level where learners shall have the opportunity to focus on
pathways, tracks and subjects of their choices guided by the potentials demonstrated at earlier levels. The Senior School shall; therefore, form a
foundation for further education and training and/or initial competencies for the Industry. This is an important step in the realisation of the Vision
and Mission of the curriculum reforms as enshrined in the Sessional Paper No. I of 2019 whose title is: Towards Realizing Quality, Relevant and
Inclusive Education and Training for Sustainable Development in Kenya.

The Grade 10 curriculum designs, like the designs for earlier levels, are anchored on the Kenyan National Goals of Education. They also present
essence statements, general and specific expected learning outcomes as well as strands and sub strands for the learning areas. The designs also outline
suggested learning experiences, key inquiry questions, core competencies, Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCIs), values and suggested
assessment.

The Ministry of Education, through the State Department for Basic Education commits to provide resources and relevant guidelines for a smooth
implementation of the CBC. It is expected that the designs will guide teachers to effectively facilitate learners to attain the expected learning outcomes
for Grade 10 specifically and Senior School in general.

NATIONAL GOALS OF EDUCATION
Education in Kenya should:
1. Foster nationalism and patriotism and promote national unity.
Kenya’s people belong to different communities, races and religions, but these differences need not divide them. They must be able to
live and interact as Kenyans. It is a paramount duty of education to help young people acquire this sense of nationhood by resolving
conflicts and promoting positive attitudes of mutual respect which enable them to live together in harmony and foster patriotism in order
to make a positive contribution to the life of the nation.

2. Promote the social, economic, technological and industrial needs for national development.
Education should prepare the youth of the country to play an effective and productive role in the life of the nation.
a) Social Needs
Education in Kenya must prepare children for changes in attitudes and relationships which are necessary for the smooth progress of a
rapidly developing modern economy. There is bound to be a silent social revolution following in the wake of rapid modernization.
Education should assist our youth to adapt to this change.
b) Economic Needs
Education in Kenya should produce citizens with the skills, knowledge, expertise and personal qualities that are required to support a
growing economy. Kenya is building up a modern and independent economy which is in need of an adequate and relevant domestic
workforce.
c) Technological and Industrial Needs
Education in Kenya should provide learners with the necessary skills and attitudes for industrial development. Kenya recognizes the
rapid industrial and technological changes taking place, especially in the developed world. We can only be part of this development
if our education system is deliberately focused on the knowledge, skills and attitudes that will prepare our young people for these
changing global trends.

3. Promote individual development and self-fulfilment
Education should provide opportunities for the fullest development of individual talents and personality. It should help children to develop
their potential interests and abilities. A vital aspect of individual development is the building of character.

v

4. Promote sound moral and religious values.
Education should provide for the development of knowledge, skills and attitudes that will enhance the acquisition of sound moral values
and help children to grow up into self-disciplined, self-reliant and integrated citizens.

5. Promote social equity and responsibility.
Education should promote social equality and foster a sense of social responsibility within an education system which provides equal
educational opportunities for all. It should give all children varied and challenging opportunities for collective activities and corporate
social service irrespective of gender, ability or geographical environment.

6. Promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures.
Education should instill in the youth of Kenya an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in contemporary society.
Children should be able to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must follow rapid development in order
to build a stable and modern society.

7. Promote international consciousness and foster positive attitudes towards other nations.
Kenya is part of the international community. It is part of the complicated and interdependent network of peoples and nations. Education
should therefore lead the youth of the country to accept membership of this international community with all the obligations and
responsibilities, rights and benefits that this membership entails.

8. Promote positive attitudes towards good health and environmental protection.
Education should inculcate in young people the value of good health in order for them to avoid indulging in activities that will lead to
physical or mental ill health. It should foster positive attitudes towards environmental development and conservation. It should lead the
youth of Kenya to appreciate the need for a healthy environment.

vi

THE SENIOR SCHOOL IN THE COMPETENCY BASED CURRICULUM
Senior School is the fourth level of Basic Education in the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) that learners shall proceed to after the Pre-
Primary School, Primary School and Junior School levels. The essence of Senior School is to offer learners a pre-tertiary/university/pre-career
experience in which the learners have an opportunity to choose pathways, tracks and subjects where they shall have demonstrated interest
and/or potential at the earlier levels. Senior School comprises three years of education for learners generally in the 16-18 years age bracket
and lays the foundation for further education and training at the tertiary level and the world of work. In the CBC vision, learners exiting this
level are expected to be engaged, empowered and ethical citizens ready to participate in the socio-economic development of the nation.

At this level, learners shall take seven (7) learning areas as recommended by the Presidential Working Party on Educational Reforms (PWPER,
2023). These shall comprise four compulsory learning areas namely: English, Kiswahili, Essential Mathematics/Core Mathematics and
Community Service Learning (CSL). Learners will choose between Core Mathematics (for learners pursuing the Science Technology
Engineering and Mathematics Pathway) and Essential Mathematics (for learners pursuing the non-STEM pathways). The learner will select
three learning areas depending on their career choice, aptitude, interest and personality with guidance by the career teacher at Senior School.

LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR SENIOR SCHOOL
By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:
1. Communicate effectively and utilise information and communication technology across varied contexts.
2. Apply mathematical, logical and critical thinking skills for problem solving.
3. Apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve problems.
4. Exploit individual talents for leisure, self-fulfilment, career growth, further education and training.
5. Uphold national, moral and religious values and apply them in day-to-day life.
6. Apply and promote health care strategies in day-to-day life.
7. Protect, preserve and improve the environment for sustainability.
8. Demonstrate active local and global citizenship for harmonious co-existence.
9. Demonstrate appreciation of diversity in people and cultures.
10. Manage pertinent and contemporary issues responsibly.

ESSENCE STATEMENT
The Indigenous Languages curriculum design has been designed equip learners with the requisite knowledge, skills and attitudes
required to participate in various social activities and interact with each other and the environment in which they live. It builds on
the language skills of listening, speaking, reading and writing handled at the Junior School level. Grammar in use is also a key
strand in the design as it supports the development of literacy and communication skills. The course will strengthen positive
attitudes and behaviour towards active listening and speaking, as well as extensive and intensive reading in indigenous language
in anticipation of the successful discovery of information. The writing types provided such as curriculum vitae and speech writing
are tailored towards developing skills that can be applied to real-life situations and the world of work.

The learner will be exposed to multiple ways of accessing information to improve learning. They will be inspired to embrace
effective learning strategies such as carrying out oral literature projects and participating in indigenous language-based
programmes in and out of school. Consequently, learning and communicating effectively in their indigenous language will be an
added advantage. The use of the thematic language teaching will ensure that the requisite concepts, skills and attitudes are acquired
within meaningful contexts and that the learner interacts with pertinent issues at community, national and global level.

By the end of the course, the learner will be expected to have attained high proficiency in the use of their indigenous language.
This will open career opportunities in the media and other fields such as translation, publishing, research, law, teaching, indigenous
science and technologies, medicine and public relations. Learners could for instance advance their knowledge of the indigenous
language to become linguists who specialise in the development of orthographies.

x

SUBJECT GENERAL LEARNING OUTCOMES
By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:
1. express themselves confidently and appropriately in a variety of social contexts,
2. apply the use of indigenous language in various communication situations,
3. demonstrate ability to apply indigenous knowledge, culture and values in varied situations,
4. comprehend information in different contexts in the indigenous language,
5. read fluently and with comprehension in indigenous language,
6. use indigenous language to legibly write ideas and opinions in different formats,
7. enjoy communicating using a variety of cultural language strategies.

DIBAJI YA WAZIRI WA ELIMU
Serikali ya Kenya imejitolea kuhakikisha kuwa malengo ya sera kuhusu Elimu, Mafunzo na Utafiti yanatimiza malengo ya Katiba
ya Kenya ya 2010, Ruwaza ya Kenya 2030, Sera ya Mtaala ya Kitaifa 2019, Malengo ya Maendeleo Endelevu ya Umoja wa
Mataifa (SDGs) na Mikataba ya Kikanda na ya Kimataifa ambayo Kenya ni mshirika.
Katika kutekeleza lengo la Elimu ya Msingi, Wizara ya Elimu (MoE) ilianzisha mchakato wa mageuzi ambao ulisababisha
kupitishwa kwa mfumo wa Elimu ya Kiumilisi CBE) mwaka 2017. Hatua hii ilifikiwa baada ya tafiti za kina, ushirikishwaji wa
wadau, ulinganisho wa kimataifa na kuzingatia hali halisi za kijamii na kiuchumi za Karne ya 21. Mfumo wa CBE nchini Kenya
ulipitisha muundo wa 2-6-3-3, ambapo tarakimu hizo zinaonyesha idadi ya miaka ambayo wanafunzi hutumia katika viwango
mbalimbali vya Elimu ya Msingi (Chekechea, Shule ya Msingi, Shule ya Junia na Daraja ya Juu ya Shule za Upili mtawalia). CBE
ina vipengele vinne muhimu: Mtaala wa Kiumilisi (CBC), Mbinu za Ufudishaji (ufundishaji na ujifunzaji), Rasilimali, na Tathmini
ya Kiumilisi. Wizara ya Elimu husimamia utoaji wa rasilimali huku vipengele vingine (Mtaala, Mbinu za Ufudishaji na Tathmini)
vikisimamiwa na Taasisi ya Ukuzaji Mitaala Kenya (KICD), Tume ya Tume ya Kuwaajiri Walimu (TSC), na Baraza la Kitaifa la
Mitihani nchini Kenya (KNEC); mtawalia.
KICD imefanikiwa kuandaa mitaala ambayo imetumika katika utekelezaji wa Mtaala wa Kiumilisi (CBC) katika kiwango cha
Chekechea, Shule ya Msingi, Shule ya Junia na Daraja ya Juu ya Shule za Upili. Kundi la kwanza la wanafunzi wanaofanya mfumo
wa CBC litajiunga na Daraja ya Juu ya Shule za Upili (Gredi ya 10 -12) mwaka 2026. Mitaala katika kiwango hiki inatarajiwa
kuwezesha wanafunzi kupata maarifa, ujuzi, maadili na mitazamo inayofaa (umilisi) ili kuwaandaa kwa ajili ya elimu ya juu na
ulimwengu wa kazi.Ninatoa wito kwa mashirika yote ya serikali ya Kenya na wadau wengine wa elimu kutumia mitaala hii kuandaa
utekelezaji fanifu na wenye tija wa Eimu wa Kiumilisi.

i

DIBAJI YA KATIBU MKUU
Wizara ya Elimu (MoE), kupitia Idara ya Serikali ya Elimu ya Msingi, imekuwa ikitekeleza Mtaala wa Kiumilisi (CBC) tangu kupitishwa kwa
Mfumo wa Mtaala wa Elimu ya Msingi (KICD, 2017) wakati wa mkutano wa kitaifa mnamo Januari 2017. Taasisi ya Ukuzaji Mitaala Kenya (KICD)
imeandaa mitaala ambayo ilitumika katika majaribio ya awali mwaka wa 2017 na 2018 kabla kuanzishwa rasmi katika kiwango cha Shule ya
Chekechea, Shule ya Msingi (Gredi 1 hadi 3) mwaka wa 2019. Mtaala huo kisha ulianzishwa katika gredi zinazofuata kwa kutumia mikakati ya
awamu kwa awamu ili kuhakikisha mpito mzuri. Kwa sasa, kundi la kwanza la wanafunzi wa Mtaala wa Kiumilisi wako katika Gredi ya 9 – gredi
ya mwisho katika Shule ya Junia.Utekelezaji wa Elimu ya Kiumilisi pia umenufaika pakubwa kutokana na mapendekezo ya Jopo Kazi la Rais kuhusu
Mabadiliko ya Elimu (PWPER), ambayo yalitolewa mnamo Agosti 2023 na kutekelezwa kikamilifu, hasa katika kuandaa mitaala.
Gredi ya 10 ni darasa la kwanza katika Daraja ya Juu ya Shule za Upili katika Elimu ya Msingi, kiwango muhimu sana ambapo wanafunzi watapata
fursa ya kuangazia njia na mwelekeo wa masomo kulingana na vipaji na uchaguzi wao, kama ulivyoonyeshwa katika viwango vya awali. Kwa hivyo,
Daraja ya Juu ya Shule za Upili itaunda msingi wa elimu ya juu zaidi na/au ukuzaji wa umilisi wa awali kwa sekta ya viwanda. Hii ni hatua muhimu
katika kufanikisha ruwaza ya mageuzi ya mtaala, ambayo inalenga kuandaa raia waliohusishwa, wenye uwezo, na waadilifu. Ruwaza na mwito wa
Mtaala wa Kiumilisi zimebainishwa katika Sheria Nambari 1 ya mwaka 2019, yenye kichwa: Kuelekea Utekelezaji wa Elimu na Mafunzo Bora,
Yanayohusiana na Mahitaji na Yaliyojumuishi kwa Maendeleo Endelevu nchini Kenya.
Mitaala ya Gredi ya 10, kama mitaala ya viwango vya awali, imejiegemeza kwenye Malengo ya Kitaifa ya Elimu Nchini Kenya. Pia huwasilisha
kauli kiini, matokeo ya jumla na maalum pamoja na mada na mada ndogo za masomo mbalimbali. Mitaala pia inaeleza shughuli za ujifunzaji,maswali
dadisi,umilisi wa kimsingi, masuala mtambuko, maadili na mapendekezo ya tathmini.
Wizara ya Elimu, kupitia Idara ya Serikali ya Elimu ya Msingi, imejitolea kutoa rasilimali na miongozo inayofaa ili kuhakikisha utekelezaji mzuri
wa Mtaala wa Kiumilisi. Inatarajiwa kwamba mitaala hii itaongoza walimu kuhakikisha ubora wa utekelezaji wa mtaala ili kuwawezesha wanafunzi
kufanikisha matokeo maalum yanayotarajiwa katika Gredi ya 10 mahsusi na Daraja ya Juu ya Shule za Upili kwa ujumla.

MALENGO YA KITAIFA YA ELIMU NCHINI KENYA
Elimu nchini Kenya inatakiwa:
1. Kukuza na kustawisha utaifa, uzalendo na kuendeleza umoja wa kitaifa
Nchini Kenya kuna jamii zenye mila, dini na tamaduni mbalimbali lakini tofauti hizi hazifai kuzitenganisha. Lazima waweze kuishi
na kutangamana kama Wakenya. Elimu ina jukumu kuu la kuwezesha vijana kujenga hisia za uzalendo na utaifa kwa kutatua
mivutano na kukuza mielekeo chanya ya kuheshimiana. Mielekeo hii itawawezesha wanajamii kuishi pamoja kwa utangamano na
kujenga uzalendo ili kuchangia ukuaji wa taifa.
2. Kukidhi mahitaji ya kijamii, kiuchumi, kiteknolojia na viwanda yanayochangia maendeleo ya kitaifa
Elimu inafaa kuwaandaa vijana wa taifa la Kenya kutekeleza wajibu wenye umuhimu katika maisha nchini.
a) Mahitaji ya kijamii
Elimu nchini Kenya lazima iwatayarishe vijana kwa mabadiliko ya mielekeo na mahusiano ambayo yanahitajika kwa maendeleo
ya haraka ya uchumi wa kisasa. Kuna uwezekano wa kuwa na mageuzi taratibu ya kijamii kutokana na maendeleo ya haraka ya
usasa. Elimu inapaswa kuwasaidia vijana kujirekekebisha kutokana na mabadiliko haya.
b) Mahitaji ya kiuchumi
Elimu nchini Kenya inafaa kukuza raia walio na stadi, maarifa, ujuzi na sifa za kibinafsi zinazohitajika kuhimili maendeleo ya
kiuchumi. Kenya inajenga uchumi huru na wa kisasa ambao unahitaji wafanyakazi wa kutosha, walio na maarifa yanayohitajika
humu nchini.
c) Mahitaji ya kiteknolojia na ya kiviwanda
Elimu nchini Kenya inafaa kuwapa vijana stadi na mielekeo inayohitajika kwa maendeleo ya kiviwanda. Kenya inatambua
mabadiliko ya haraka ya kiviwanda na kiteknolojia yanayofanyika, hasa katika ulimwengu ulioendelea. Tunaweza kuwa
sehemu ya maendeleo haya ikiwa mfumo wetu wa elimu utalenga kimakusudi maarifa, stadi na mielekeo itakayotayarisha vijana
kwa mabadiliko yanayoendelea ulimwenguni.
3. Kutoa nafasi ya kujiendeleza na kujitosheleza
Elimu inapaswa kuwezesha kutambua, kukuza na kuimarisha vipawa vya kila mmoja ili kuweza kujiendeleza na kujitosheleza.
Inafaa kuwawezesha watoto kukuza uwezo wao. Kipengele muhimu cha maendeleo ya kibinafsi ni ujenzi wa tabia ifaayo.

vi

4. Kuwawezesha wananchi kuimarisha maadili na amali za kijamii na kidini
Elimu inakusudiwa kukuza maarifa, stadi na mielekeo itakayoimarisha upataji wa maadili na kuwasaidia watoto kukua wakiwa
wenye nidhamu, wanaojitegemea na raia wakamilifu.
5. Kuimarisha usawa wa kijamii na uwajibikaji
Usawa wa kijamii kwa mfano, usawa wa kijinsia huimarika watu wa jamii na jinsia zote wanapopata elimu sawa.
Elimu inafaa ikuze usawa wa kijamii na uwajibikaji wa kijamii kutokana na mfumo wa elimu unaowezesha fursa sawa ya elimu
kwa wote. Inafaa kuwapa watoto wote fursa mbalimbali na zenye changamoto zitakazowawezesha kutoa huduma jumuishi za
kijamii bila kujali jinsia, uwezo au mazingira ya kijiografia.
6. Kukuza uthamini wa tamaduni mbalimbali nchini Kenya
Elimu inafaa kuwapa vijana uelewa wa tamaduni za kale na za sasa na nafasi yazo katika jamii ya kisasa. Vijana wanafaa
kuambatanisha maadili ya tamaduni bora na mahitaji yanayobadilika kulingana na maendeleo yanayotokea ili kujenga jamii thabiti
ya kisasa.
7. Kuimarisha utambuzi wa uhusiano wa kimataifa na kukuza mwelekeo chanya kwa mataifa mengine
Kenya kama nchi mojawapo ya jamii ya kimataifa inakusudia elimu iwaelekeze Wakenya kutambua na kuthamini mahusiano ya
kimataifa kwa kuzingatia mikataba, uwajibikaji, haki na manufaa yanayoambatana na ushirika huo.
8. Kustawisha mwelekeo chanya kuhusu afya bora na uhifadhi wa mazingira
Elimu inakusudiwa kujenga mielekeo ifaayo miongoni mwa vijana kuhusu udumishaji wa afya bora na mazingira kwa kujiepusha
na mienendo inayoweza kudhuru afya ya mwili na akili. Aidha, inafaa kuimarisha mielekeo chanya kuhusu ukuzaji na uhifadhi wa
mazingira na kuwaelekeza vijana kuthamini usafi wa mazingira.

vii

DARAJA YA JUU SHULE ZA UPILI KATIKA MTAALA WA KIUMILISI
Daraja ya Juu ya Shule za Upili, ni kiwango cha nne cha Elimu ya Msingi katika Mtaala wa Kiumilisi (CBC) ambayo wanafunzi
watajiunga nayo baada ya kumaliza Chekechea, Shule ya Msingi, na Shule ya Junia. Lengo kuu la Daraja ya Shule za Upili ni kuwapa
wanafunzi uzoefu wa awali wa chuo kikuu au taaluma, ambapo wanafunzi wanapata fursa ya kuchagua mielekeo na nyanja
wanazovutiwa nazo na walizoonyesha uwezo katika viwango vya awali. Daraja ya Juu ya Shule za Upili inajumuisha miaka mitatu ya
masomo kwa wanafunzi walio kati ya umri wa miaka 16-18 na huweka msingi wa elimu ya juu zaidi, mafunzo ya kitaaluma, na
ulimwengu wa kazi. Katika ruwaza ya Mtaala wa Kiumilisi, wanafunzi watakaohitimu katika kiwango hiki wanatarajiwa kuwa raia
waliohusishwa, waliowezeshwa, na waadilifu walio tayari kushiriki katika maendeleo ya kijamii na kiuchumi ya taifa.
Katika kiwango hiki, wanafunzi watajifunza masomo saba (7) kama yalivyopendekezwa na Kamati ya Rais ya Mageuzi ya Elimu
(PWPER, 2023). Masomo haya yanajumuisha masomo manne ya lazima ambayo ni: English, Kiswahili, Essential Mathematics/Core
Mathematics na Community Service Learning – CSL. Wanafunzi watachagua kati ya Core Mathematics (kwa wanafunzi wanaofuatilia
mkondo wa STEM) na Essential Mathematics (kwa wanafunzi wanaofuatilia mikondo isiyo ya STEM). Wanafunzi watachagua masomo
mengine matatu kulingana na chaguo la taaluma, vipaji, mapendeleo yao kwa somo fulani, na haiba zao, wakisaidiwa na mwalimu wao
wa Daraja ya juu shule za upili.
MATOKEO YA DARAJA YA JUU SHULE ZA UPILI
Kufikia mwisho wa Daraja ya Juu ya Shule za Upili, mwanafunzi aweze:
1. Kuwasiliana ipasavyo na kutumia teknolojia ya habari na mawasiliano katika miktadha mbalimbali.
2. Kutumia maarifa ya kihisabati, kimantiki na uwazaji kina katika utatuzi wa matatizo.
3. Kutumia maarifa ya kimsingi ya utafiti na sayansi kudhibiti mazingira yake na kutatua matatizo.
4. Kutumia vizuri vipaji mbalimbali kwa ajili ya burudani, kujiendeleza kitaaluma, kielimu pamoja na kimafunzo.
5. Kudumisha tunu za kitaifa, kimaadili na kidini katika maisha ya kila siku.
6. Kutumia na kuendeleza mikakati ya matunzo ya kiafya katika maisha ya kila siku.
7. Kulinda, kuhifadhi na kuboresha mazingira kwa ajili ya uendelevu.
8. Kudhihirisha uraia wa kitaifa na wa kimataifa kwa ajili ya utangamano wa kindugu.
9. Kuonyesha uthamini wa tofauti za watu na tamaduni.
10. Kuonyesha uwajibikaji katika kushughulikia masuala mtambuko.

KAULI KIINI
Somo la Kiswahili katika Daraja ya Juu ya Shule za Upili linaendeleza maarifa, ujuzi na stadi ambazo mwanafunzi amepata katika
Shule ya Junia. Lengo kuu ni kumwezesha mwanafunzi kupanua uelewa na umilisi wake wa lugha ya Kiswahili, si tu kama somo,
bali pia kama chombo cha kumwezesha kuyafahamu mazingira yake, kudumisha mahusiano yafaayo ya kijamii na kushirikiana
na tamaduni anuwai. Somo hili linashughulikia stadi nne za lugha, Kusikiliza, Kuzungumza, Kusoma na Kuandika, pamoja na
matumizi ya lugha ambayo yanajumuisha Sarufi na Isimujamii. Vipengele vilivyoshughulikiwa kama vile kuzungumza kwa
kushawishi, kusikiliza na kujibu mjadala, kuzungumza kwa kupasha habari, na uzungumzaji husishi, miongoni mwa vingine,
vinamwimarishia mwanafunzi stadi za kimawasiliano huku zikimkuzia stadi za karne ya ishirini na moja kama vile uwazaji kina
na utatuzi wa matatizo. Mada ya Isimujamii nayo inampa mwanafunzi stadi za kutumia lugha ipasavyo katika miktadha mbalimbali
ya kijamii, hivyo kumjengea umilisi wa kimsingi kama vile uraia. Kadhalika, somo hili linamkuzia mwanafunzi ubunifu, huku
likimpa mbinu za kushirikiana na wenzake kitaifa na kimataifa.
Ujifunzaji wa Kiswahili katika kiwango hiki unalenga kumjengea mwanafunzi msingi wa taaluma atakayofuata katika vyuo vya
kati na vyuo vikuu, na hapo hapo kumtayarisha kwa ulimwengu wa ajira. Shughuli mbalimbali za ujifunzaji kama vile mijadala,
uzungumzaji wa papo kwa hapo, uandishi wa tungo amilifu kama vile ripoti na kumbukukumbu, pamoja na kushiriki katika
kazimradi, hazichangii tu kumkuzia mwanafunzi ufasaha wa lugha, bali pia kumpa nafasi ya kujitathmini na kubaini ubora na
udhaifu wake.
Kufikia mwisho wa kozi, mwanafunzi anatarajiwa kwamba atakuwa amefikia kiwango cha juu cha umahiri katika lugha ya
Kiswahili. Somo hili linamtayarisha mwanafunzi kwa taaluma mbalimbali zikiwemo taaluma ya habari na mawasiliano,
ufundishaji na sheria. Somo hili linamfungulia mwanafunzi fursa za ajira katika vyombo vya habari na nyanja nyingine kama vile
ufundishaji, utafiti, uchapishaji, sanaa, burdani, tafsiri na ukalimani. Umilisi wa lugha hii pia unachangia kufanikisha utoaji wa
huduma katika taaluma nyingine kama vile udaktari na uhandisi ambazo zinamhitaji mtaalamu kutagusana na wateja wake kwa
lugha wanayoelewa.

MATOKEO YA KIJUMLA YA SOMO LA KISWAHILI KATIKA DARAJA YA JUU YA SHULE ZA UPILI
Kufikia mwisho wa Daraja ya juu ya Shule ya Upili, mwanafunzi aweze:
1. kusikiliza kwa makini na kuitikia ipasavyo kwa Kiswahili katika miktadha mbalimbali ya mawasiliano,
2. kujieleza ipasavyo kimaandishi na kimazungumzo kwa kuzingatia kanuni za lugha ya Kiswahili,
3. kuwasiliana ipasavyo katika miktadha mbalimbali ya kijamii,
4. kusoma kwa ufasaha na kufasiri matini mbalimbali zilizochapishwa na za kidijitali ili kupata ujumbe,
5. kutumia teknolojia ipasavyo katika ujifunzaji na mawasiliano ili kukuza ujuzi wa kidijitali,
6. kutumia maadili yanayohitajika maishani kupitia stadi za lugha ya Kiswahili,
7. kuonea fahari lugha ya Kiswahili kama lugha rasmi, ya taifa na kimataifa.

FOREWORD
The Government of Kenya (GoK) is committed to ensuring that policy objectives for Education, Training and Research meet the aspirations
of the Kenya Constitution 2010, the Kenya Vision 2030, National Curriculum Policy 2019, the United Nations Sustainable Development
Goals (SDGs) and the Regional and Global conventions to which Kenya is a signatory.
Towards achieving the mission of Basic Education, the Ministry of Education (MoE) embarked on a reform process that culminated in the
adoption of a Competency Based Education (CBE) system in 2017. This came after extensive research, stakeholder engagement international
benchmarking and consideration of the 21st Century socio-economic realities. CBE in Kenya adopted a 2-6-3-3 structure where the numbers
indicate the years learners take at various levels in Basic Education (Pre-Primary, Primary, Junior School and Senior School; respectively).
CBE has for critical elements: The Competency Based Curriculum (CBC), Pedagogy (teaching and learning), Resources and the Competency
Based Assessment. The MoE oversees the provision of resources while the other components (Curriculum, Pedagogy and Assessment are
handled by the Kenya Institute of Curriculum Development, (KICD), Teachers Service Commission, (TSC) and the Kenya National
Examinations Council (KNEC); respectively.
KICD has successfully developed curriculum designs that have been used in the implementation of the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC)
for the Pre-Primary, Primary and Juniors School levels. The first cohort of learners pursuing the CBC will transit to Senior School (Grades
10-12) in 2026. The curriculum designs at this level are expected to facilitate learners to acquire relevant knowledge, skills, values and attitudes
(competencies) in preparation for tertiary education and the world of work. I urge all agencies of the GoK and other stakeholders in Education
to use the designs to plan for effective and efficient implementation of Competency Based Education.

MR. JULIUS MIGOS OGAMBA
CABINET SECRETARY,

PREFACE
The Ministry of Education (MoE) through the State Department for Basic Education, has been implementing the Competency Based Education
(CBE) since the adoption of the Basic Education Curriculum Framework (KICD, 2017) during the national convention in January 2017. The Kenya
Institute of Curriculum Development (KICD) developed Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) designs that were used for pilot studies in 2017 and
2018 before the roll-out at Pre-Primary and Primary Early Year (Grades 1 to 3 in 2019. The curriculum was then introduced in the subsequent grades
through a phase in –phase out strategy, to ensure a smooth transition. Currently, the first cohort of CBC learners are at Grade 9 – the last grade at
Junior School. The implementation of CBE has since benefited immensely from the recommendations of the Presidential Working Party on
Education Reforms (PWPER) that were released in August, 2023 and fully implemented, in terms of curriculum designs.
Grade 10 is the entry class of the Senior School (SS) in Basic Education, a very critical level where learners shall have the opportunity to focus on
pathways, tracks and subjects of their choices guided by the potentials demonstrated at earlier levels. The Senior School shall; therefore, form a
foundation for further education and training and/or initial competencies for the Industry. This is an important step in the realisation of the Vision
and Mission of the curriculum reforms as enshrined in the Sessional Paper No. I of 2019 whose title is: Towards Realizing Quality, Relevant and
Inclusive Education and Training for Sustainable Development in Kenya.
The Grade 10 curriculum designs, like the designs for earlier levels, are anchored on the Kenyan National Goals of Education. They also present
essence statements, general and specific expected learning outcomes as well as strands and sub strands for the learning areas. The designs also outline
suggested learning experiences, key inquiry questions, core competencies, Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCIs), values and suggested
assessment.
The Ministry of Education, through the State Department for Basic Education commits to provide resources and relevant guidelines for a smooth
implementation of the CBC. It is expected that the designs will guide teachers to effectively facilitate learners to attain the expected learning outcomes
for Grade 10 specifically and Senior School in general.

NATIONAL GOALS OF EDUCATION
Education in Kenya should:
1. Foster nationalism and patriotism and promote national unity.
Kenya’s people belong to different communities, races and religions, but these differences need not divide them. They must be able
to live and interact as Kenyans. It is a paramount duty of education to help young people acquire this sense of nationhood by
resolving conflicts and promoting positive attitudes of mutual respect which enable them to live together in harmony and foster
patriotism in order to make a positive contribution to the life of the nation.
2. Promote the social, economic, technological and industrial needs for national development.
Education should prepare the youth of the country to play an effective and productive role in the life of the nation.
a) Social Needs
Education in Kenya must prepare children for changes in attitudes and relationships which are necessary for the smooth progress
of a rapidly developing modern economy. There is bound to be a silent social revolution following in the wake of rapid
modernization. Education should assist our youth to adapt to this change.
b) Economic Needs
Education in Kenya should produce citizens with the skills, knowledge, expertise and personal qualities that are required to
support a growing economy. Kenya is building up a modern and independent economy which is in need of an adequate and
relevant domestic workforce.
c) Technological and Industrial Needs
Education in Kenya should provide learners with the necessary skills and attitudes for industrial development. Kenya recognizes
the rapid industrial and technological changes taking place, especially in the developed world. We can only be part of this
development if our education system is deliberately focused on the knowledge, skills and attitudes that will prepare our young
people for these changing global trends.
3. Promote individual development and self-fulfilment
Education should provide opportunities for the fullest development of individual talents and personality. It should help children to
develop their potential interests and abilities. A vital aspect of individual development is the building of character.

vi

4. Promote sound moral and religious values.
Education should provide for the development of knowledge, skills and attitudes that will enhance the acquisition of sound moral
values and help children to grow up into self-disciplined, self-reliant and integrated citizens.
5. Promote social equity and responsibility.
Education should promote social equality and foster a sense of social responsibility within an education system which provides
equal educational opportunities for all. It should give all children varied and challenging opportunities for collective activities and
corporate social service irrespective of gender, ability or geographical environment.
6. Promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures.
Education should instil in the youth of Kenya an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in contemporary
society. Children should be able to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must follow rapid
development in order to build a stable and modern society.
7. Promote international consciousness and foster positive attitudes towards other nations.
Kenya is part of the international community. It is part of the complicated and interdependent network of peoples and nations.
Education should therefore lead the youth of the country to accept membership of this international community with all the
obligations and responsibilities, rights and benefits that this membership entails.
8. Promote positive attitudes towards good health and environmental protection.
Education should inculcate in young people the value of good health in order for them to avoid indulging in activities that will
lead to physical or mental ill health. It should foster positive attitudes towards environmental development and conservation. It
should lead the youth of Kenya to appreciate the need for a healthy environment.

vii

THE SENIOR SCHOOL IN THE COMPETENCY BASED CURRICULUM
Senior School is the fourth level of Basic Education in the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) that learners shall proceed to after the Pre-
Primary School, Primary School and Junior School levels. The essence of Senior School is to offer learners a pre-tertiary/university/ pre-career
experience in which the learners have an opportunity to choose pathways, tracks and subjects where they shall have demonstrated interest
and/or potential at the earlier levels. Senior School comprises three years of education for learners generally in the 16-18 years age bracket
and lays the foundation for further education and training at the tertiary level and the world of work. In the CBC vision, learners exiting this
level are expected to be engaged, empowered and ethical citizens ready to participate in the socio-economic development of the nation.
At this level, learners shall take seven (7) learning areas as recommended by the Presidential Working Party on Educational Reforms (PWPER,
2023). These shall comprise four compulsory learning areas namely: English, Kiswahili, Essential Mathematics/Core Mathematics and
Community Service Learning (CSL). Learners will choose between Core Mathematics (for learners pursuing the Science Technology
Engineering and Mathematics Pathway) and Essential Mathematics (for learners pursuing the non-STEM pathways). The learner will select
three learning areas depending on their career choice, aptitude, interest and personality with guidance by the career teacher at Senior School.
LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR SENIOR SCHOOL
By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:
1. Communicate effectively and utilise information and communication technology across varied contexts.
2. Apply mathematical, logical and critical thinking skills for problem solving.
3. Apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve problems.
4. Exploit individual talents for leisure, self-fulfilment, career growth, further education and training.
5. Uphold national, moral and religious values and apply them in day-to-day life.
6. Apply and promote health care strategies in day-to-day life.
7. Protect, preserve and improve the environment for sustainability.
8. Demonstrate active local and global citizenship for harmonious co-existence.
9. Demonstrate appreciation of diversity in people and cultures.
10. Manage pertinent and contemporary issues responsibly.

ESSENCE STATEMENT
The study of Literature in Senior School builds upon the foundational language and literary skills acquired at Junior School under
the integrated approach. This stage marks a significant transition, where learners begin to engage with more complex literary texts
and themes that reflect societal values, human experiences, and diverse cultures. As a pre-career stage, Senior School offers
learners the opportunity to refine their communication skills, critical thinking, empathy, and creativity—attributes that are vital
across numerous professional fields. Literature, therefore, becomes a key discipline in nurturing learners who are not only
academically competent but also socially aware and ethically grounded.
In line with CBC principles, the teaching and learning of Literature in Senior School is crafted to be learner-centred and activity-
based, promoting autonomy and discovery. Learners are encouraged to take ownership of their learning through guided reading,
group discussions, dramatisation, performance, and fieldwork projects and activities such as theatre visits and storytelling sessions.
Emphasis is placed on “learning to learn,” where students develop metacognitive skills, reflective habits, and the ability to apply
literary knowledge in varied contexts. Writing remains a core component, with learners engaging in creative and analytical writing
tasks that foster expression, interpretation, and critique. Assessment is continuous and performance-based, allowing for holistic
development.
By the time learners exit Senior School, they should demonstrate a well-rounded profile that includes advanced communication
skills, cultural literacy, ethical sensitivity, and creative expression. These competencies prepare them not only for tertiary education
but also for the dynamic world of work. Literature opens pathways to a range of careers such as teaching, journalism, publishing,
theatre arts, law, media, and communication. Moreover, the study of Literature equips learners with the soft skills and emotional
intelligence required in any professional setting, fostering adaptable, thoughtful, and articulate individuals ready to contribute
meaningfully to society.

xi

GENERAL SUBJECT LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR LITERATURE IN ENGLISH
By the end of the course, the learner should be able to:
1. Critically analyse literary texts and relate them to real life experiences
2. Apply literary terms and devices effectively in school and real life
3. Develop critical thinking skills for problem solving
4. Apply digital literacy skills to enhance the learning, production and enjoyment of literature
5. Appreciate skills to understand human nature and emotions as brought out in literature and real life
6. Develop research skills for lifelong learning of literature
7. Acquire skills for the creation, performance and preservation of literature for study, self-expression, enjoyment and for the
good of society
8. Appreciate literature in its various forms and relate it to human experiences and values.

FOREWORD
The Government of Kenya (GoK) is committed to ensuring that policy objectives for Education, Training and Research meet the aspirations
of the Kenya Constitution 2010, the Kenya Vision 2030, National Curriculum Policy 2019, the United Nations Sustainable Development
Goals (SDGs) and the Regional and Global conventions to which Kenya is a signatory.
Towards achieving the mission of Basic Education, the Ministry of Education (MoE) embarked on a reform process that culminated in the
adoption of a Competency Based Education (CBE) system in 2017. This came after extensive research, stakeholder engagement international
benchmarking and consideration of the 21st Century socio-economic realities. CBE in Kenya adopted a 2-6-3-3 structure where the numbers
indicate the years learners take at various levels in Basic Education (Pre-Primary, Primary, Junior School and Senior School; respectively).
CBE has for critical elements: The Competency Based Curriculum (CBC), Pedagogy (teaching and learning), Resources and the Competency
Based Assessment. The MoE oversees the provision of resources while the other components (Curriculum, Pedagogy and Assessment are
handled by the Kenya Institute of Curriculum Development, (KICD), Teachers Service Commission, (TSC) and the Kenya National
Examinations Council (KNEC); respectively.
KICD has successfully developed curriculum designs that have been used in the implementation of the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC)
for the Pre-Primary, Primary and Juniors School levels. The first cohort of learners pursuing the CBC will transit to Senior School (Grades
10-12) in 2026. The curriculum designs at this level are expected to facilitate learners to acquire relevant knowledge, skills, values and attitudes
(competencies) in preparation for tertiary education and the world of work. I urge all agencies of the GoK and other stakeholders in Education
to use the designs to plan for effective and efficient implementation of Competency Based Education.

MINISTRY OF EDUCATION

PREFACE
The Ministry of Education (MoE) through the State Department for Basic Education, has been implementing the Competency Based Education
(CBE) since the adoption of the Basic Education Curriculum Framework (KICD, 2017) during the national convention in January 2017. The Kenya
Institute of Curriculum Development (KICD) developed Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) designs that were used for pilot studies in 2017 and
2018 before the roll-out at Pre-Primary and Primary Early Year (Grades 1 to 3 in 2019. The curriculum was then introduced in the subsequent grades
through a phase in –phase out strategy, to ensure a smooth transition. Currently, the first cohort of CBC learners are at Grade 9 – the last grade at
Junior School. The implementation of CBE has since benefited immensely from the recommendations of the Presidential Working Party on
Education Reforms (PWPER) that were released in August, 2023 and fully implemented, in terms of curriculum designs.
Grade 10 is the entry class of the Senior School (SS) in Basic Education, a very critical level where learners shall have the opportunity to focus on
pathways, tracks and subjects of their choices guided by the potentials demonstrated at earlier levels. The Senior School shall; therefore, form a
foundation for further education and training and/or initial competencies for the Industry. This is an important step in the realisation of the Vision
and Mission of the curriculum reforms as enshrined in the Sessional Paper No. I of 2019 whose title is: Towards Realizing Quality, Relevant and
Inclusive Education and Training for Sustainable Development in Kenya.
The Grade 10 curriculum designs, like the designs for earlier levels, are anchored on the Kenyan National Goals of Education. They also present
essence statements, general and specific expected learning outcomes as well as strands and sub strands for the learning areas. The designs also outline
suggested learning experiences, key inquiry questions, core competencies, Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCIs), values and suggested
assessment.
The Ministry of Education, through the State Department for Basic Education commits to provide resources and relevant guidelines for a smooth
implementation of the CBC. It is expected that the designs will guide teachers to effectively facilitate learners to attain the expected learning outcomes
for Grade 10 specifically and Senior School in general.
